sources.title: METR: task-completion time horizons
sources.date: Page updated May 8, 2026; data retrieved Sep 20, 2026
sources.limits: Selected releases: May 2024–Feb 2026. Narrow domains and wide uncertainty. See archived raw data.

sources.title: OSWorld 2.0
sources.limits: 108 long computer workflows; maximum 500 steps in cited result. New task set; scores cannot be compared directly with OSWorld 1.0.

sources.title: OpenAI: GDPval
sources.limits: 1,320 tasks, 44 occupations. Measures supplied-context work products; does not establish full-job substitution. Publisher sells the evaluated technology.

sources.title: Epoch AI: inference price trends
sources.method: Independent analysis of benchmark and API price data
sources.limits: Historical price at fixed performance. Different benchmarks yield different rates; excludes deployment and human costs.

sources.title: Census: business AI use, December 2025–May 2026
sources.limits: US employer businesses. Any business function, previous two weeks. November 17, 2025 question change breaks comparison with earlier narrower series.

sources.title: Census: The Microstructure of AI Diffusion
sources.limits: Firm and employment weights answer different questions. Adoption and business outcomes are reported, not randomized.

sources.title: Federal Reserve: Monitoring AI Adoption in the U.S. Economy
sources.method: Primary survey comparison and methodological analysis
sources.limits: BTOS, RPS and SBU cover different populations, reference periods and definitions. Employment weighting is not a worker-use rate.

sources.title: Eurostat: Digitalisation in Europe 2026
sources.limits: Survey covers enterprises with at least 10 workers in covered sectors. Excludes microbusinesses; not directly comparable with US BTOS.

sources.title: Bick et al.: What Work Does Generative AI Do?
sources.limits: Nationally representative worker survey linked to tasks. Self-reported use; exposure and platform chat categories do not measure the same thing.

sources.title: Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond: Generative AI at Work
sources.limits: 5,172 support agents at one firm. Updated published estimate is 15%; do not mix with earlier 14% working-paper version.

sources.title: Cui et al.: AI and software developer productivity
sources.limits: 4,867 developers. Pooled effect of adoption estimated using randomized access; 26.08%, standard error 10.3 percentage points. Company-level estimates are noisy; Microsoft-affiliated coauthors.

sources.title: Dillon et al.: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
sources.date: AER: Insights, forthcoming; abstract accessed September 20, 2026
sources.method: Randomized field experiment; accepted article abstract
sources.limits: 66 firms, 7,137 workers, six months. Two-hour estimate concerns users in the second half, not all assigned workers. Microsoft-affiliated coauthors.

sources.title: Dell’Acqua et al.: The Cybernetic Teammate
sources.method: Randomized innovation exercise; author abstract and HBS researcher account
sources.limits: 776 P&G professionals in this version. Short product-development exercise; does not measure enduring team replacement. P&G supported the research.

sources.title: METR: early-2025 developer experiment
sources.limits: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 tasks in familiar repositories. Time increase 19%, 95% interval 2%–39%. Narrow and dated setting.

sources.title: METR: developer-productivity follow-up
sources.limits: 57 developers, 800+ tasks. Participation and task selection changed; both reported subgroup intervals cross zero. Not a clean estimate of current average gains.

sources.title: METR: AI usage survey
sources.limits: 349 respondents; selected sample. Perceived counterfactual speed and value are not experimentally measured output.

sources.title: Humlum & Vestergaard: Still Waters, Rapid Currents
sources.date: March 13, 2026 version; two years after ChatGPT launch
sources.method: Working paper; surveys linked to administrative records
sources.limits: Danish difference-in-differences estimates. Null average earnings/hours effects do not rule out task change, later effects or different outcomes elsewhere.

sources.title: Yotzov et al.: Firm Data on AI
sources.limits: Nearly 6,000 executives across US, UK, Germany and Australia. Retrospective impact is self-reported. Future expectations are not observed results.

sources.title: Atlanta Fed, Richmond Fed & Duke: CFO evidence
sources.limits: Reported output-per-worker gains exceed gains implied by reported revenue and headcount. Neither measure is an audited causal estimate.

sources.title: McKinsey: The State of AI in 2026
sources.limits: 36% work at firms with over $1bn revenue; country-GDP weighting. Self-reported use and impact, not representative of all firms by count. Publisher sells AI consulting.

sources.title: OECD: Generative AI and the SME Workforce
sources.method: Representative telephone survey; 5,232 SMEs in seven countries
sources.limits: Includes one-person businesses through 249 employees. Barrier percentages refer to non-adopters; multiple answers allowed. Older adoption snapshot, not September 2026 prevalence.

sources.title: DBS: agentic credit-assessment rollout
sources.limits: 150-person pilot followed by rollout to about 1,500 staff. The 30% time reduction is a goal, not a measured result. No controlled outcomes disclosed.

sources.title: IBM CHRO: redesigning HR service delivery
sources.limits: Channel closures, policy simplification and automation changed together. Reported containment and budget changes do not isolate generative AI. IBM also sells these systems.

sources.title: Jabarian & Henkel: Voice AI in Firms
sources.method: Randomized field experiment; full methods reviewed
sources.limits: Philippine entry-level service recruitment; human hiring authority retained. Google Cloud support. One author later accepted an unpaid role at the partner firm.

sources.title: He et al.: AI Writes Faster Than Humans Can Review
sources.limits: Nonrandom adoption. The 2.09× statistic counts authored pull requests per active developer, distinct from the mandate’s merged-output target. Quality proxies miss latent defects.

sources.title: DBS: platforms, processes and people
sources.limits: Reported delivery-time reduction accompanies shared data and model infrastructure. No counterfactual or cost breakdown; large-bank infrastructure may not transfer economically to an SME.

sources.title: Klarna: 2025 Form 20-F
sources.method: Company regulatory filing; narrative disclosures, PDF page 188
sources.limits: 80% chat share and approximately $59m savings are company-reported measures. A filing is not independent causal validation of AI savings; customers retained human support.

sources.title: Google Cloud: 2025 DORA findings
sources.method: Primary research summary; survey of nearly 5,000 technology professionals
sources.limits: Reported associations, not random assignment. More AI use correlated with both throughput and instability. Google Cloud sells AI and development products.

sources.title: DBS: customer assistants and agentic rollout
sources.limits: Joy outcomes precede its July agentic upgrade. Eligible users are not active users. Satisfaction baseline and causal contribution are undisclosed.

sources.title: DBS: 2025 CEO reflections
sources.limits: Economic value covers data analytics and all AI/ML, not just generative AI. Program counts and management estimates are not controlled returns.

sources.title: Permanente: ambient AI scribe deployment
sources.method: Deploying institution’s account of its NEJM Catalyst study
sources.limits: Observational adoption and patient surveys. Primary institutional summary reviewed; journal full text was inaccessible. No demonstrated increase in patient capacity or profit.

sources.title: DBS: 2024 CIO statement
sources.method: Management account of process and control changes
sources.limits: Manual hours are cumulative; incident reductions have different definitions. Digitalization and conventional ML are included. These are not isolated generative-AI effects.

revision_scope: Deepened operational cases and measured outcomes; added DBS customer service, bank-wide implementation evidence and Permanente clinical documentation.
